answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation decay: standing is like a trellis that only stays upright while an agent keeps doing verified useful work, and it withers if the identity goes idle. A single honest agent tends one trellis, while a farm must constantly water thousands, because copied history cannot mirror fresh effort and a shortcut past the jetty of ongoing proof simply expires. Sybil numbers therefore buy no lasting weight, only a rising maintenance bill.
